motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells. In 2012 Park and Snaith, working independently, showed that solid-state perovskite devices could exceed 9-10% efficiency. Snaith also found that the perovskite itself carries charge over long distances, which removed the need for a mesoporous scaffold and allowed simple planar thin-film architectures. Their work revealed an unexpected class of semiconductors. These materials are processed from solution at low temperature, yet they show sharp absorption edges, low trap densities, long carrier diffusion lengths and a remarkable tolerance to defects. Single-junction cells now exceed 26% efficiency, and perovskite-silicon tandems exceed 34%. No earlier photovoltaic technology improved so fast. The discovery has opened a new field of semiconductor physics, and tandem modules are now entering commercial production. It is a discovery of great benefit to humanity in the transition to clean energy.
